correctness.rationale: Block spectral decomposition and convex automorphism averaging give the known exact scalar optimum. For s<=2r, saturation of the negative contrast eigenvalue forces uniform between-part row/column sums, and saturation of all outer-difference Rayleigh quotients forces B=xJ. For s>2r, saturation of total clique row capacity and the exact trace of the outer-difference compression force B=xJ and a zero core. Orthogonal decomposition yields a necessary-and-sufficient semidefinite core face. Trace/eigenvalue and diagonal bounds yield sharp T endpoints; constant-offdiagonal feasible cores attain the entire interval. Executed exact checker verified 217 rational cases, six symbolic characteristic polynomials, eight noninvariant core examples and forced-edge examples. A computer test is supporting evidence, not the proof.

The accepted claim is narrower but stronger in its quantifiers: full characterization of all globally optimal kernels with no imposed symmetry, exact obligatory cross-edge equality, the remaining semidefinite core face, and a sharp internal-edge traffic interval. value.rationale: A fully solved optimum rate alone does not say which individual communication links must be used, nor whether the design is unique. The two-parameter exact classification provides an all-optima spectral face, forces every cross edge to identical probability for ANY optimizer, and gives a sharp tripartite phase boundary for the necessity of clique communication. This answers a natural design-degeneracy question for an unbounded named graph family and quantitatively describes a complete range of permissible internal traffic; not a numerical recomputation of the known rate.
